capability_1_binary_release.description: Release is BINARY (full transition or no transition) — deterministic, no partial state
capability_1_binary_release.M3_mechanism: SMA phase transition is thermodynamic — at T_sma > Af, full transition occurs in milliseconds. No partial release state.
capability_1_binary_release.A4_limitation: Cryo-debonding depends on cold SALINE DIFFUSION through tissue — diffusion is gradual, non-uniform. Partial freezing possible at interface edges. Release may be incomplete if cold saline doesn't reach all adhesion points.
capability_1_binary_release.importance: HIGH — incomplete release means anchor doesn't detach, retrieval fails. V3 Monte Carlo showed M3 achieves 98.7% reliability; A4 estimated 95% (3.7pp gap).

capability_2_release_without_catheter_ad.description: Release triggered WITHOUT advancing a catheter to the implant-tissue interface
capability_2_release_without_catheter_ad.M3_mechanism: SMA is integrated into permanent implant. Triggered by external inductive heater or resistive heater. No catheter advancement needed.
capability_2_release_without_catheter_ad.A4_limitation: Cold saline must be delivered via catheter to implant-tissue interface. Catheter advancement through venous sinus risks vessel injury, dissection, thrombus formation.
capability_2_release_without_catheter_ad.importance: HIGH — venous sinus anatomy is curved, fragile. Catheter advancement risk is a real clinical concern. M3 eliminates this risk entirely.

capability_3_pre_positioned_release_mech.description: Release mechanism is PRE-POSITIONED at implantation — operator only triggers, doesn't position
capability_3_pre_positioned_release_mech.M3_mechanism: SMA element is built into the eShunt at manufacture. At retrieval, operator triggers; no positioning needed.
capability_3_pre_positioned_release_mech.A4_limitation: Cold saline catheter must be POSITIONED at the implant-tissue interface under fluoroscopy. Positioning takes 5-15 minutes of fluoroscopy time, requires skilled operator.
capability_3_pre_positioned_release_mech.importance: MEDIUM — procedural complexity, fluoroscopy exposure, operator skill requirement.

capability_4_self_test_capability.description: Release mechanism can be SELF-TESTED before final activation (verify it will work)
capability_4_self_test_capability.M3_mechanism: SMA can be pulsed with low-energy thermal pulse (below full activation threshold) to verify transition occurs. Impedance change confirms SMA is functional.
capability_4_self_test_capability.A4_limitation: Cannot test cryo-debonding without actually delivering cold saline — once tested, the adhesion is broken. No 'dry-run' possible.
capability_4_self_test_capability.importance: HIGH — clinical workflow benefits from pre-activation verification. Reduces failed-retrieval risk.

capability_5_zero_catheter_inventory_req.description: Retrieval requires NO specialty catheter inventory (just a standard retrieval sheath)
capability_5_zero_catheter_inventory_req.M3_mechanism: SMA triggered by external magnetic field or RF — no specialized catheter needed. Standard retrieval sheath suffices.
capability_5_zero_catheter_inventory_req.A4_limitation: Requires specialized cold saline delivery catheter (insulated, with distal infusion ports). Hospital must stock this catheter. Cost: ~$2000-5000 per procedure.
capability_5_zero_catheter_inventory_req.importance: MEDIUM — hospital inventory, cost, training burden.

capability_6_selective_anchor_release_on.description: Release ONLY the anchor — shunt body and other structures remain intact for clean retrieval
capability_6_selective_anchor_release_on.M3_mechanism: SMA element is specifically at the anchor-shunt body junction. Activation detaches ONLY the anchor.
capability_6_selective_anchor_release_on.A4_limitation: Cold saline diffuses to ALL tissue in contact with implant. May weaken adhesion at multiple points, not just anchor. Risk of shunt body shifting during retrieval.
capability_6_selective_anchor_release_on.importance: MEDIUM — clean retrieval requires controlled release point.

capability_7_no_permanent_material_modif.description: No permanent implant material modification needed (no SMA, no isolation layer added to implant)
capability_7_no_permanent_material_modif.M3_limitation: M3 permanently adds SMA + isolation layer to eShunt. Increases implant profile, complexity, manufacturing cost.
capability_7_no_permanent_material_modif.importance: MEDIUM — implant profile, regulatory burden, manufacturing cost.

capability_8_universal_applicability.description: Can be used on ANY endovascular implant (not just eShunt) — cold saline works on any fibrotic interface
capability_8_universal_applicability.M3_limitation: M3 requires SMA to be designed INTO the implant at manufacture. Cannot be retrofitted to existing implants.
capability_8_universal_applicability.importance: LOW for CereVasc (eShunt-specific invention), HIGH for broad applicability

capability_9_lower_manufacturing_cost.description: Lower per-implant manufacturing cost (no SMA, no isolation)
capability_9_lower_manufacturing_cost.M3_limitation: SMA + isolation layer adds ~$500-2000 per implant manufacturing cost
capability_9_lower_manufacturing_cost.importance: MEDIUM — cost pressure on medical devices

m3_critical_advantages_summary: No catheter advancement (eliminates vessel injury risk in venous sinus)
ceo_question_answer.ceo_question_answer: YES — M3's critical advantages (binary release reliability, no catheter advancement in venous sinus, self-test capability, selective release) are CLINICALLY IMPORTANT and A4 CANNOT reproduce them. A4's advantages (no permanent modification, lower cost) are MANUFACTURING/COMMERCIAL, not clinical. For a CereVasc buyer (clinical优先), M3's clinical advantages outweigh A4's commercial advantages. The thermal/implant complexity IS justified by clinical capability differences.
ceo_question_answer.caveat: HOWEVER — A4's lower manufacturing cost could be decisive if CereVasc's reimbursement environment is cost-constrained. The 5-axis comparison in Stage 4 separates these concerns.

tighter_tolerance_pm1C.regulatory_burden: INCREASED — custom processing requires additional validation

tolerance_decision.decision: STANDARD TOLERANCE ACCEPTABLE — standard ±2°C tolerance gives 4.55% failure rate (1 in 21 implants fails to activate within T4 limit). For a retrieval device used in <5% of patients (most eShunts never need retrieval), this failure rate is acceptable. Tighter ±1°C tolerance adds $525.0 per implant (28.9%) applied to ALL implants to save <0.5% retrieval failures — NOT cost-effective. MITIGATION: Pre-retrieval SELF-TEST (M3 unique capability) identifies failed-SMA implants BEFORE attempting retrieval — if self-test fails, fall back to standard snare retrieval. This makes the 4.55% failure rate MANAGEABLE without tighter tolerance.

axis_1_engineering_superiority.reasoning: M3 has BINARY release (98.7% reliability vs 95% A4 estimated), SELF-TEST capability (A4 cannot self-test), SELECTIVE anchor-only release (A4 non-selective). A4 has lower complexity but lacks critical engineering capabilities. M3 wins on engineering capability; A4 wins on simplicity.
evidence: V3 Monte Carlo: M3 98.7% retrieval success
V4 chronic attack: M3 SURVIVES 60 months

axis_2_section_103_differentiation.reasoning: M3 has MODERATE §103 risk (Excimer Laser Sheath E1 is near-neighbor; thermal isolation distinguishes but is combination of known elements). A4 has LOW §103 risk (no direct prior art on cryo-debonding for implant retrieval). A4 wins on §103 differentiation — cleaner novelty position.
evidence: V4 A4 prior-art check: no direct prior art

axis_3_manufacturability.reasoning: M3 requires SMA + thermal isolation layer integrated into permanent implant. Standard tolerance cost: $1819.0/implant. Tighter tolerance (if needed): $2344.0/implant (+28.9%). A4 has no permanent implant modification — only requires disposable cold saline catheter. A4 wins on manufacturability — lower implant cost, no specialized SMA processing.
evidence: A4: no implant modification, only disposable catheter

axis_4_chronic_safety.reasoning: M3 chronic safety: V4 60-month attack SURVIVES (T_tissue_peak 39.35°C, margin 7.65°C). BUT M3 has chronic risks: SMA aging (Af drift +0.5°C/5yr — manageable), polyimide degradation (k_iso 1.63x at 60mo — manageable), fibrotic capsule (offsets degradation). A4 chronic safety: NO permanent implant modification → NO chronic material degradation risks. A4 has only ACUTE risks (catheter advancement, cold saline exposure) which are procedural, not chronic. A4 wins on chronic safety — no permanent implant burden.
evidence: V4 M3 chronic: SURVIVES 60 months but with degradation

axis_5_buyer_value.reasoning: Buyer = CereVasc (clinical优先). M3 provides: binary release reliability (98.7%), no catheter advancement risk in venous sinus, self-test capability, selective release. These are CLINICAL advantages that A4 cannot reproduce. A4 provides: lower manufacturing cost, lower §103 risk, no permanent modification. These are COMMERCIAL advantages. For a CereVasc buyer prioritizing clinical outcomes, M3's clinical advantages outweigh A4's commercial advantages. M3 wins on buyer value — but narrowly (8.0 vs 7.0).
evidence: M3 clinical: 98.7% reliability, no catheter advancement, self-test
A4 commercial: lower cost, lower §103 risk

stage_5_adjudication.verdict: PARALLEL_DEVELOPMENT. M3 (7.20) and A4 (7.40) are within 0.5 points — too close to call. M3 wins on engineering/buyer axes; A4 wins on §103/manufacturability/chronic axes. BOTH candidates retained for parallel V6 development. Decision deferred to V6 benchtop data.
